volume: Heidegger and Rhetoric (Gross & Kemmann eds., SUNY 2005)
compiled_from: 8 Phase 2 unit JSONs (HR-01-GROSS-A, HR-01-GROSS-B, HR-02-GADAMER, HR-03-MICHALSKI, HR-04-HYDE, HR-05-STRUEVER, HR-06-KISIEL, HR-07-POGGELER)
methodology_note: Each disagreement maps two or more contributor positions onto a shared topical axis with productive divergence. Sub-disagreements (e.g., DG6a, DG6b) capture finer-grained productive splits. By-omission disagreements (where one contributor's silence is itself a position) are flagged in the type field.

disagreements.topic: Centrality of rhetoric to Heidegger's mature thought (rhetoric central vs. restricted)

position_a.label: Centrality — rhetoric relocates at the heart of fundamental ontology
position_a.claim: Heidegger's SS 1924 reading of Aristotle's Rhetoric is constitutively formative for Being and Time and for fundamental ontology as such; the GA 18 110 identification ('Rhetoric is nothing other than the interpretation of concrete Dasein, the hermeneutic of Dasein itself') is a load-bearing positive endorsement of rhetoric as ontological medium; ten BT signature terms (Mitsein/koinonia, Glaube/doxa, Lage, Sorge, Stimmung/pathos, Augenblick/kairos, ekstasis, Angst/phobos, logos, Entschluss/krisis) have rhetorical genealogy.
key_evidence: Gross Intro p.4 (italicized): 'Heidegger thus relocates rhetoric at the heart of his fundamental ontology' (HR-01-GROSS-A-P2)
Gross Intro p.2: BT 158 cites Aristotle's Rhetoric as source of the concernful-understanding-to-theory dynamic; ten-term glossary (HR-01-GROSS-A-P1)
Hyde p.82, p.88, p.95: BT 178 anchor as positive Heidegger acknowledgment that Aristotle Rhetoric II is 'first systematic hermeneutic of everydayness of Being-with-one-another' (HR-04-HYDE-P1, P2)
Struever p.105 (epigraph), p.117, p.122, p.126: Rhetoric 'colonizes Being and Time' — manifold-temporality, Befindlichkeit, Sorge, Sein-zum-Tode all genetically rhetorical (HR-05-STRUEVER-P8)
Kisiel p.131-133, p.139-141: rhetorical protopolitics 'equiprimordial' with threefold definition of human; constitutive of fundamental ontology at level of everyday speech-situation (HR-06-KISIEL-P1)
Gadamer p.49, p.60: 'It is the same dynamis!' — rhetoric as dynamis IS the universal human capacity for speaking-understanding (HR-02-GADAMER-P1, P5)

position_b.label: Restriction — rhetoric is a bounded Marburg episode, not a constitutive concept of mature thought
position_b.claim: Heidegger's serious engagement with rhetoric is circumscribed to the Marburg lecture courses 1923-28 (especially GA 18 SS 1924); rhetoric is ABSENT from Aus der Erfahrung des Denkens (1947), Letter on Humanism (1947), Der Satz vom Grund (1957), the Trakl essay (1953), and Unterwegs zur Sprache (1959). The mature 'topology of being' (Topologie des Seyns), the Geviert, and the turn to Hölderlin/Heraclitus replace rather than continue the rhetorical engagement. 'Restriction' is both temporal (Marburg-bounded) and substantive (Heidegger curtails rhetoric's deliberative-public dimension even within Marburg).
key_evidence: Pöggeler titular: 'Heidegger's Restricted Conception of Rhetoric' (HR-07-POGGELER-P1)
Pöggeler p.161-163: 1947 Aus der Erfahrung des Denkens introduces 'topology of being' — rhetoric ABSENT from this work

Pöggeler p.171-172: Letter on Humanism's animal rationale / Hölderlin / polemic against 'dictatorship of publicness' simultaneously polemicize against polis-orientation of rhetoric (HR-07-POGGELER-P4)

Pöggeler p.168: Heidegger's BT §29 hermeneutic-of-everydayness reading IS the moment of restriction — confines political to das Man / Öffentlichkeit, surrenders deliberative-public dimension (HR-07-POGGELER-P2, P7)
Pöggeler p.166-167: WS 1925-26 lecture course renamed FROM 'Aristotle: Rhetoric' TO 'Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy' — rename itself a restriction (HR-07-POGGELER-P3)

disagreements.synthesis: The volume's architecture stages this disagreement: Gross opens with centrality, Pöggeler closes with restriction. Both cite GA 18 SS 1924 — yet the same text yields opposite verdicts because the contributors track in opposite temporal directions. Pöggeler tracks BACKWARD from 1947 (post-Marburg, post-rhetoric) and finds the Marburg engagement a bounded episode that the topology of being supplants. The other six contributors track FORWARD from 1924 (Marburg, rhetorical) and find the SS 1924 → BT genetic line constitutive. Pöggeler concedes (P5) that even when hidden, Heidegger 'touches the rhetorical tradition again and again' — the hiddenness is itself the productive layer. The two positions are not symmetric: the centrality cluster makes constitutive claims that the restriction thesis can dent but not refute (the GA 18 → BT trajectory IS textually attested); the restriction thesis makes architectural claims that the centrality cluster cannot easily absorb (the topology of being, the Geviert, the turn to poetics ARE post-rhetorical). The productive synthesis Gross himself anticipates (Section IV p.41): rhetoric-as-named-discipline is dropped in late Heidegger, but rhetoric-as-ontological-grammar persists; the depoliticization-by-hermeneutics thesis actually PREDICTS Pöggeler's restriction reading as a symptom of the post-1924 trajectory.
disagreements.dissertation_relevance: DG1 is the volume's master tension and the master productive disagreement for any dissertation arguing a sustained Aristotelian-rhetorical strand in Heidegger. The dissertation cannot evade Pöggeler's restriction claim — the textual evidence for the post-Marburg shift is real (Topologie, Geviert, Hölderlin-turn). Best dissertation strategy: distinguish rhetorical-named-discipline (which Heidegger does drop) from rhetorical-ontological-grammar (which the GA 18 → BT trajectory continues, however attenuated, into post-1933 Heidegger). The disagreement also surfaces a methodological point: scholarly readings of Heidegger are tracking-direction-sensitive — the choice of starting-point (1947 vs. 1924) constitutes the verdict.

disagreements.topic: Rhetoric as dynamis vs. as technē — what does it mean to define rhetoric ontologically?

position_a.label: Rhetoric as dynamis — power belonging to being-human (consensus-with-volume)
position_a.claim: Aristotle's Rhetoric I.2 defines rhetoric correctly as dynamis (power, capacity), not as technē (art, craft); Heidegger's SS 1924 / GA 18, 114 explicitly designates the technē-construal 'incorrect' and the dynamis-construal correct. Rhetoric-as-dynamis is universal human capacity-for-speaking-and-understanding ('everyone is a speaker'), aligns rhetoric with energeia rather than productive-poietic craft, and protects rhetoric from instrumentalization.
key_evidence: Gadamer p.49: 'Heidegger said it: that designation [of rhetoric as technē] is incorrect... dynamis is the proper definition' (GA 18, 114 cited) (HR-02-GADAMER-P1)
Gadamer p.60: 'It is the same dynamis!' — rhetoric as dynamis IS hermeneutics' dynamis IS being-human's understanding capacity (HR-02-GADAMER-P5)
Struever p.108, p.116, p.122: rhetoric is 'not a technē' but 'dynamis tou theoresai' (potentiality-for-theorizing) — Rhet. 1355b26 / GA 18 122 (HR-05-STRUEVER-P3)
Kisiel p.146: 'rhetoric is first of all not an art but a power, dynamis' (HR-06-KISIEL-P1, T9-cross)

position_b.label: (Implicit) Tradition default — rhetoric as technē (no contributor explicitly defends; absence is the productive layer)
position_b.claim: The rhetorical tradition treats rhetoric as technē — productive-poietic craft, an art transmittable in handbooks (Hellenistic, medieval, Ramist school discipline). Aristotle himself elsewhere designates rhetoric as technē — Heidegger and Gadamer must therefore privilege ONE Aristotelian text (Rhet. I.2 dynamis-definition) against another (Aristotle's elsewhere-technē-designation). Pöggeler implicitly preserves part of this position via his observation that Heidegger 'starts from a definition of these concepts' (Aristotle's) rather than building a constructive rhetorical concept (HR-07-POGGELER-P3).
key_evidence: Gadamer p.49 acknowledges the textual fact: 'Aristotle himself elsewhere designates rhetoric as technē' — the technē-tradition is real, Heidegger's choice is interpretive
Struever p.108: 'inauthentic definition' Heidegger rejects (GA 18 114) IS the tradition's technē-construal

Pöggeler p.166-167 (HR-07-POGGELER-P3): the Marburg engagement is rhetorical 'only because it was a PHILOLOGICAL Aristotle interpretation' — the dynamis-reading is Heidegger's PHILOLOGICAL choice between two Aristotelian designations, not a constructive rhetorical concept

sub_disagreement_DG2a.label: Gadamer's internal correction — Heidegger 'missed' the technē side
sub_disagreement_DG2a.claim: Gadamer (p.49) adds a subtle correction: 'Heidegger was still using technē, until he began emphatically using the concept of energeia. And so he associated the concept of dynamis with the concept of energeia, and missed the other one [technē as productive-poietic dimension].' This is a Gadamer-internal qualification of the volume's consensus dynamis-reading — Heidegger's choice protects rhetoric from instrumentalization but at the cost of the productive-poietic dimension Aristotle himself preserves.

disagreements.synthesis: The volume's consensus on dynamis is unusually strong — six of seven contributors affirm it explicitly or tacitly. The productive layer is the ABSENCE of a defender of technē: the unified dynamis-reading marks the volume's distance from the post-Aristotelian rhetorical tradition (school discipline, handbook craft) Heidegger repudiates. Yet Gadamer's internal correction (DG2a) flags what is lost in the unified reading: the productive-poietic dimension that the technē-designation preserves. The dissertation can mine this productive split — the dynamis-reading licenses an ontological-existential rhetoric, the missed technē-side gestures at a productive-poietic dimension (rhetor as maker-of-arguments) that fuller Aristotle-reading would also need to recover.
disagreements.dissertation_relevance: DG2 is load-bearing for any dissertation that wants to define rhetoric ontologically (in Heideggerian register) without collapsing it into a hermeneutic capacity-for-listening that loses rhetoric's productive-active dimension. Gadamer's DG2a correction is the dissertation-actionable lever: a recovered rhetorical-ontology must preserve BOTH dynamis (capacity, universal) AND a recovered productive sense of technē-as-poiesis (not as Ramist handbook-craft, but as Aristotelian making-of-arguments).

disagreements.topic: Continuity vs. rupture in Heidegger 1924-1927-post-1933 — does the SS 1924 → BT trajectory smoothly genetic or substantively interrupted?

position_a.label: Strong continuity — SS 1924 is genetically formative for BT 1927; substantive carryover
position_a.claim: SS 1924 GA 18 is one of Heidegger's greatest courses, breaking ground 'not merely in Greek philosophy but also for his entire path of thought' (Kisiel's Genesis cited via Gross n.6). The ten BT terms have rhetorical genealogy; BT §§29-30 (Befindlichkeit, fear) explicitly cite Aristotle Rhetoric II via SS 1924; BT 178 endorses Aristotle Rhetoric II as 'first systematic hermeneutic of everydayness of Being-with-one-another'; BT's manifold-temporality, Befindlichkeit, Sorge, Sein-zum-Tode all have SS 1924 rhetorical-Aristotelian genesis. The continuity reading makes SS 1924 a constitutive moment for BT, not a station Heidegger eventually leaves.
key_evidence: Gross Intro p.2 citing Kisiel: SS 1924 'provides us with perhaps our best glimpse into how that book on Aristotle might have looked' (HR-01-GROSS-A-P1)
Hyde p.83: Heidegger 'takes up this task in his 1924 lecture course and especially in Being and Time' (HR-04-HYDE-P2)
Struever p.117 (Section II.2 opening): SS 1924 lectures 'explain' BT 1927 — manifold-temporality and Alltäglichkeit genetic (HR-05-STRUEVER-P8)
Michalski p.76-77: SS 1924 lectures 'finally wound up being systematically drafted in Sein und Zeit, published in 1927' — continuous moment in trajectory (HR-03-MICHALSKI-T7)

position_b.label: Continuity-with-substantive-loss — genetic line affirmed but BT depoliticizes / mutes the rhetorical-political
position_b.claim: BT inherits SS 1924 genetically but loses the rhetorical-political dimension; Heidegger 'dropped his earlier convictions that public speaking could authentically emerge from political community' (book p.40). Befindlichkeit replaces pathē but with conceptual loss; Heidegger moves 'decisively out of the emotional public sphere and into the rarefied domain of the resolute Freeman' (BT 434). The hermeneutic turn coincides with depoliticization of Heidegger's rhetorical thinking. The 1933 turn (Rectoral Address, support for Hitler) is the political-philosophical consequence of having lost (between 1924 and 1933) the rhetorical-political resources Heidegger himself discovered in SS 1924.
key_evidence: Gross IV p.40, p.41: BT 'dropped his earlier convictions that public speaking could authentically emerge from political community' (HR-01-GROSS-B-P8)
Gross IV p.39-40: 1933 Heidegger's Nietzsche-reading (Heidegger Nietzsche I 48-49) — pluralist rhetoric of 1924 replaced by 'great-will-superiority' (HR-01-GROSS-B-P9)
Gross IV p.41: depoliticization-by-hermeneutics — modern speech-act theory (Grice, Searle, Habermas, Sperber) inherits the impoverished post-1924 disposition (HR-01-GROSS-B-P10)

position_c.label: Three-phase succession — protopolitical → metontological → archaic-poietic (continuity displaced, not lost)
position_c.claim: Heidegger's three concepts of polis form a strict succession in which only the FIRST is rhetorical: Phenomenological (1923-25, Aristotle's Rhetoric — pathos/ethos/logos), Metontological (1933-35, Plato's Republic — leader-guardians-services), Archaic-Poietic (1935-43, Sophocles' Antigone — polemos). Rhetoric is progressively displaced — by the will-of-the-Führer (Phase 2) and by the polemos-of-poetic-origin (Phase 3). Each phase has a 'basic text' and 'basic concepts'; the displacement is itself rhetorically traceable (GA 53 102: language as 'original institution of being in violent words of poetic origin' rather than 'means of communication for sake of quick easy agreement, rhetoric'). The Nazi turn is a phronetic miscalculation traceable to Heidegger's own framework: Heidegger applies his 1924 phronesis-framework to the inauthentic-doxa-rhetoric of the Führer state he had earlier diagnosed.
key_evidence: Kisiel table p.149 (three-phase polis): SS 1924 / Aristotle Rhetoric / pathos-ethos-logos; WS 1933-34 / Plato Republic / leader-guardians-three-services; GA 39 + GA 53 / Sophocles Antigone / polemos (HR-06-KISIEL-P2)
Kisiel p.149-151: Heidegger's 1933 'Schlageter speech' and Rectoral Address are inauthentic-doxa applications of his own framework (HR-06-KISIEL-P3)
Kisiel p.151-153: GA 53 102 — post-1935 language as polemos abandons rhetoric proper (HR-06-KISIEL-P4)

position_d.label: Rupture / abandonment — post-1924 trajectory toward poetics, topology of being abandons rhetoric
position_d.claim: Pöggeler tracks 1947 backward and finds the topology of being abandons rhetoric. Post-1947 Heidegger turns to Hölderlin/Trakl/Heraclitus; the Geviert (fourfold) crystallizes a poetic-cosmic place-figure, not a rhetorical-argumentative one. The 'topology of being' is structurally distinct from the rhetorical topics tradition (Aristotle's topoi, Cicero's loci, Vico). Heidegger's December 1958 letter to Pöggeler explicitly brackets 'historical connotations' of 'topology' — i.e., the rhetorical-topical tradition is refused. Even where the rhetorical tradition is touched (Erörterung, late truth-of-language), the relation is one of buried debt, not theoretical inheritance.
key_evidence: Pöggeler p.161-163: 1947 Aus der Erfahrung des Denkens introduces topology of being; rhetoric absent from this and from Letter on Humanism (HR-07-POGGELER-P1, P6)
Pöggeler p.171-172: late Heidegger 'touches the rhetorical tradition again and again' but as buried debt (HR-07-POGGELER-P5)
Pöggeler n.28: WS 1925-26 course renamed FROM 'Aristotle: Rhetoric' TO 'Basic Concepts' — the rename itself a restriction (HR-07-POGGELER-P3)

disagreements.synthesis: Four distinct positions on the same axis. Gross-B's continuity-with-loss reading is the most nuanced: he affirms genetic continuity with Kisiel (a vs. Pöggeler) but joins Pöggeler in flagging substantive loss (b vs. Hyde-Struever-Michalski). Kisiel's three-phase model is the volume's most articulated mediating position — affirms continuity (rhetoric IS in Phase 1) while affirming displacement (rhetoric is NOT in Phases 2-3). The four positions can be productively triangulated: Gross-B + Kisiel + Pöggeler agree on substantive post-1924 attenuation; Hyde, Struever, Michalski track only the SS 1924 → BT line and do not foreground the post-BT trajectory. The disagreement is generative because the underlying textual record IS staged: BT 178 / GA 18 110 affirm rhetoric; Letter on Humanism distances from rhetoric; Aus der Erfahrung des Denkens introduces topology. The textual data supports BOTH continuity (1924 → BT) AND rupture (BT → late Heidegger). The dissertation must navigate both — the cleanest move is Kisiel's three-phase succession with Gross-B's substantive-loss diagnosis layered onto Phases 2-3.
disagreements.dissertation_relevance: DG3 is the structural map for any dissertation argument that traces Heideggerian rhetoric through the corpus. Kisiel's three-phase table (p.149) is the most useful single artifact: it disciplines the diachronic reading by naming the textual basis of each phase. Gross-B's depoliticization-thesis adds the political-philosophical stakes (the 1933 turn is not biographically contingent but framework-consequent). Pöggeler's restriction-thesis prevents complacent continuity-readings. The dissertation can integrate all four positions by accepting Kisiel's textual map, Gross-B's political diagnosis, Hyde-Struever-Michalski's SS 1924 → BT genetic claim, and Pöggeler's late-Heidegger abandonment-of-rhetoric — these are compatible at different layers.

disagreements.topic: Politics — protopolitical vs. tragic-acknowledgement vs. erred-but-disconnected vs. silent

position_a.label: Affirmative protopolitics — rhetorical protopolitics already in 1923-24
position_a.claim: Heidegger's SS 1924 (and pre-Marburg) work develops a 'rhetorical protopolitics' equiprimordial with the threefold definition of human (logon echon, zoon politikon, practical being-in-world). The everyday speech-situation IS the political situation of being-with-one-another. The Nazi turn is a phronetic miscalculation INTERNAL to Heidegger's own 1924 framework — Heidegger mistook the Trommelnder-Führer-rhetoric for kairos-grasping civic rhetoric. The framework is salvageable; the 1933-1935 application is internally diagnostic of failure. Arendt's Human Condition recovers the protopolitical strand of GA 18 without ever directly accessing GA 18 — by radicalizing Mitwelt as plurality-natality space.
key_evidence: Kisiel p.132: 'rhetorical protopolitics' already in 1923-24 (HR-06-KISIEL-P1)
Kisiel p.149-151: Schlageter speech / Rectoral Address as phronetic miscalculation (HR-06-KISIEL-P3)
Kisiel p.153-156: Arendt as redemptive afterlife of protopolitical strand (HR-06-KISIEL-P5)
Struever p.123-125: 'Heideggerian politics of time appears, even if briefly, in SS 1924' — Arendt's early fascination (HR-05-STRUEVER-P9)

position_b.label: Tragic-acknowledgement — rhetoric is political, Heidegger's Nazism IS framework-consequent
position_b.claim: Rhetoric is political through-and-through (Gross Intro pp.5, 39-40). Heidegger's 1933 turn is not biographically contingent but the political-philosophical consequence of having lost the rhetorical-political resources he himself discovered in SS 1924. The body politic gets subordinated to 'the so-called great will' in Heidegger's 1930s Nietzsche reading. Gross treats the Nazi turn as a tragedy of philosophical loss: the same Heidegger who in 1924 articulated rhetorical pluralism (proto-Arendtian) abandoned that very pluralism by 1933.
key_evidence: Gross Intro pp.5, 39-40: rhetoric is political; 'subsequent Nazism' addressed (HR-01-GROSS-A-P3)
Gross IV pp.39-40: 1933 Heidegger and 1930s Nietzsche-reading — pluralism replaced by great-will (HR-01-GROSS-B-P9)
Gross IV p.41: depoliticization-by-hermeneutics — political-ethical 'loss' (HR-01-GROSS-B-P10)

position_c.label: Erred-but-disconnected — Heidegger erred politically but the error is not framework-consequent
position_c.claim: Heidegger 'erred when he did this' (the rectorate); the political mistake created distance between Heidegger and Gadamer (book p.55). Heidegger occupied his rectorate for less than a year — a fact Gadamer insists on stating 'at every opportunity.' The political retreat coincided with Heidegger's poetics-only turn (Hölderlin, Trakl). Gadamer concedes the political error but does NOT connect it to rhetoric specifically; footnote 31 refers to Gadamer's own 'Über die politische Inkompetenz der Philosophie' for the longer treatment. Hyde's Section V (epideictic-conscience absent, agriculture/extermination equation) is closer to Gross's tragic-acknowledgement reading but operates at a more specifically rhetorical-ethical register.
key_evidence: Gadamer p.55: 'erred' political acknowledgment; less-than-one-year rectorate (HR-02-GADAMER-P9)
Gadamer p.56: post-political poetics-only turn — Hölderlin, Trakl, Celan (HR-02-GADAMER-T3)
Hyde p.97-99: 'a sincere concern for the truth and goodness of rhetoric disappeared from view' — Heidegger 1949 'agriculture/extermination camp' equation as rhetorical-ethical failure (HR-04-HYDE-P7)

position_d.label: Silent — no direct discussion of 1933 in the closing essay (by-omission position)
position_d.claim: Pöggeler's opening locates 1947 as 'troubled year' (Heidegger 'indicted on account of his National Socialist entanglement') but the indictment is the OCCASION for Aus der Erfahrung des Denkens, not its substantive theme. Letter on Humanism is read for its poetic-elemental Kehre, not its political evasiveness. Heidegger's 'unable to confront the published reports of his actions in 1933' is mentioned (p.171) but not developed. Pöggeler's silence is itself a position: the topology of being supplants both rhetoric AND politics.
key_evidence: Pöggeler p.161 (opening): 1947 as 'troubled year' — indictment mentioned but undeveloped
Pöggeler p.171: Heidegger 'unable to confront the published reports of his actions in 1933' — single mention
Pöggeler HR-07-POGGELER-T5: by-omission diagnosis — 'the topology of being supplants both rhetoric AND politics'

disagreements.synthesis: Four distinct positions span the volume; Kisiel's three-phase table on p.149 is the most articulated single position. The most productive tension is between Kisiel's protopolitics-as-framework-consequent reading (the Nazi turn IS phronesis miscalculation INTERNAL to Heidegger's own 1924 framework) and Gadamer's erred-but-disconnected reading (the political error does NOT impeach the philosophy). Gross-B sits structurally with Kisiel on the framework-consequent thesis but offers a different mechanism (depoliticization-by-hermeneutics rather than phronesis-miscalculation). Pöggeler's silence frames the volume's closing — the contributor whose 'restricted conception' thesis would seem most amenable to political diagnosis declines to develop it. The disagreement is productive because it stages the very question dissertation work on Heidegger's politics must engage: is the Nazi turn philosophically consequent or biographically contingent?
disagreements.dissertation_relevance: DG4 is essential for any dissertation that wants to address Heidegger's Nazism without either evading it (Gadamer-Pöggeler) or reducing his whole thought to it (anti-Heideggerian readings). The Kisiel-Gross synthesis — Nazi turn as framework-consequent (Kisiel) for reasons of depoliticization-by-hermeneutics (Gross-B) — is the most defensible scholarly position the volume itself articulates. Pöggeler's silence is dissertation-actionable: if a 'restricted conception' thesis declines to develop the political consequence, then the centrality cluster (Kisiel, Gross) has more dissertation-purchase on the political stakes.

disagreements.topic: Pathos as cognitive resource vs. ontological substrate — what does Heidegger's pathē-as-Befindlichkeit do?

position_a.label: Pathos as cognitive-rhetorical resource — orator deploys pathē deliberately
position_a.claim: Aristotle's pathē are deliberate rhetorical resources for the orator (orator must 'put his hearers into the right frame of mind'); pathē are constituents of judgment (krisis), not noise. The Heideggerian Ruf des Gewissens operates structurally as primordial epideictic rhetoric — a silent, ontologically-prior showing-forth (epideixis) of the heart of human existence. Hyde keeps the orator's intentional structure intact: pathē are 'rooted in the emotional fabric of a person's existence' AND deployed by the orator. The enthymeme's audience-completion function bridges to Heidegger's 'sich etwas zu Herzen nehmen' (GA 18 128) — taking-to-heart names the emotional/cognitive dual register.
key_evidence: Hyde p.84, p.88, p.90: pathē as constituents of judgment, deliberate rhetorical resources (HR-04-HYDE-P1, P2)
Hyde p.86-88: anger, fear, pity 'restructure existential temporality and spatiality' — orator deploys (HR-04-HYDE-P4)
Hyde p.88-90: enthymeme audience-completion via 'taking-to-heart' (HR-04-HYDE-P5)
Hyde T3 self-acknowledgment: 'Hyde's orator-position is closer to Aristotle's NE phronimos'

position_b.label: Pathos as ontological substrate — pre-cognitive ground of logos, dissolves orator into Befindlichkeit
position_b.claim: Pathos is 'the very substance in which propositional thought finds its objects and motivation' (Gross Intro p.4) — pre-cognitive ontological substrate. The pathē are not psychology but ontology; the eidos of the pathē is 'a disposition toward other humans, a Being-in-the-world' (GA 18 207). Without pathos, there would be no traffic between inside and outside, self and Other, individual and community; pathos is what makes humans subject-to-movement (Sein in Bewegung). Gross dissolves the orator into pre-cognitive Befindlichkeit: pathos is the structural condition for logos, not a resource logos deploys.
key_evidence: Gross Intro p.4: pathos as 'the very substance' (HR-01-GROSS-A-P10)
Gross IV p.36: 'Without pathos, no traffic between inside and outside' (HR-01-GROSS-B-P5)
Gross IV p.27, 30, 36-41: pathē-as-condition-of-krisis, not as embellishment (HR-01-GROSS-B-P1, P5)

position_c.label: Productive middle — pathē as pre-articulate ground AND bewährt (warranted) grounds-for-judgment
position_c.claim: Heidegger SS 1924 establishes pathē as 'fundamental possibilities by which Dasein primarily orients itself, is attuned' (GA 18, 117); they are the ground of logos and have argumentative power that is bewährt — warranted, not arbitrary. Speaking is not 'first': Sich-Befinden precedes articulation. But pathos is bewährt — warranted, not arbitrary; this protects the thesis from collapse into pure-affective relativism. Betroffensein (being-affected) is the pre-articulate condition Gadamer claims as his own advance beyond Heidegger. Gadamer's reading sits closer to Gross's substrate-reading than to Hyde's deliberate-resource-reading; but the bewährt caveat preserves the argumentative function pathē perform — partial alignment with Hyde.
key_evidence: Gadamer p.57-58 (Section IV): pathē as 'fundamental possibilities' grounding logos (HR-02-GADAMER-P3)
Gadamer p.58: bewährt caveat — argumentative power warranted, not arbitrary (HR-02-GADAMER-P3)
Gadamer T6 synthesis: 'productive middle' between Gross and Hyde

position_d.label: Pathos relegated to attunement — Heidegger LOSES Aristotle's rhetorical pathē at the BT moment
position_d.claim: Heidegger's gloss in GA 18: ethos = Haltung (attitude); pathos = Befindlichkeit (one's feeling of attunement). This is the moment Heidegger SUBSTITUTES an existential-ontological category (Befindlichkeit) for the rhetorical category (pathos), thereby LOSING the pathos-as-rhetorical-resource that the orator deliberately deploys. The pathetic / pathic is 'relegated' to attunement and mood; rhetoric's claim on pathos is dissolved into the existential structure of being-in-the-world. When Heidegger 'ceases any longer to set passions and feelings over against virtues,' he leaves behind not only Aristotle but also Scheler. Pöggeler's reading FORECLOSES both Hyde's epideictic preservation AND Gross's substrate-reading: Hyde's BT-§§54-60 conscience-analysis is precisely where rhetoric is LOST, not preserved.
key_evidence: Pöggeler p.169: pathos = Befindlichkeit; pathē 'relegated' to attunement (HR-07-POGGELER-P2)

Pöggeler P2 targets: 'Hyde's reading that Heidegger's call of conscience operates ontologically as a primordial and emotional form of epideictic rhetoric — Pöggeler's premise (b) and (c) imply that the BT-§§54-60 conscience-analysis is precisely where rhetoric is LOST, not preserved'
Pöggeler P2 targets: 'Gross's reading that pathos is the very substance — Pöggeler reads BT §29 as the moment Heidegger SUBSTITUTES Befindlichkeit for pathos'

disagreements.synthesis: Four positions on one axis. Hyde's cognitive-resource reading and Gross's ontological-substrate reading are not incompatible at different layers (Hyde: rhetorical-genre-level; Gross: existential-ontological-level), but they operate at different registers and yield different downstream commitments. Gadamer's bewährt-caveat occupies the productive middle: pathē are pre-articulate (Gross-side) but argumentatively warranted (Hyde-side). Pöggeler's reading is the structural antagonist of both Hyde and Gross: he reads the Befindlichkeit-substitution as the LOSS of rhetorical pathē, not as their preservation in ontological register. The disagreement is generative because it surfaces a downstream stakes-question: when Heidegger glosses Aristotelian pathos as Befindlichkeit, is that translation a preservation (Hyde, Gross), a transformation (Gadamer), or a dissolution (Pöggeler)?
disagreements.dissertation_relevance: DG5 is critical for any dissertation that uses pathos as a load-bearing concept in a Heideggerian register. The translation pathē → Befindlichkeit is the dissertation's most consequential terminological move. Hyde's reading allows a dissertation to preserve rhetorical-genre distinctions (epideictic vs. deliberative vs. forensic) at the existential-ontological level. Gross's reading produces a more ambitious ontological claim (pathos as constitutive of community-as-such) but at the cost of the orator's distinct intentional structure. Gadamer's bewährt-caveat is the most defensible middle position. Pöggeler's loss-thesis is the negative case the dissertation must address — and addressing it requires a textual argument that Befindlichkeit-translation preserves what matters about pathos (not merely renames it).

disagreements.topic: Hermeneutic displacement of rhetoric — substantive loss vs. continuous engagement
disagreements.type: intra-volume-direct-engagement (Gross interrogates Gadamer; Gadamer responds via interview)

position_a.label: Substantive loss — hermeneutics displacing rhetoric entails a political and ethical loss
position_a.claim: The displacement of rhetoric by hermeneutics — exemplified by Gadamer's Truth and Method — entails a 'political and ethical loss' that, while not absolute, is real and that 'depoliticizes' the priority of pathos. Gadamer 'downplays' the loss (Intro p.5); rhetoric is 'depoliticized' with the turn (Intro p.6). Gadamer 'cedes ground... to the very rationalists [Habermas] he sets out to criticize' by claiming understanding-precedes-affect; Gadamer 'chooses not to reclaim for rhetoric the doctrine of affections (Affektenlehre) as taught by the likes of Luther or Schleiermacher.' Modern speech-act theory (Grice, Searle, Habermas, Sperber) inherits the impoverished post-1924 disposition — power gets 'swept' into 'amorphous backgrounds of unarticulated predispositions.'
key_evidence: Gross Intro p.5: 'political and ethical loss'; Gadamer 'downplays' (HR-01-GROSS-A-P3)
Gross Intro pp.5-9: T&M depoliticization (HR-01-GROSS-A-P3)
Gross IV p.41: speech-act theory inheritance (HR-01-GROSS-B-P10)

position_b.label: Continuous engagement — hermeneutics IS rhetoric properly understood; conceptual coextension with institutional modesty
position_b.claim: Gadamer's interview position: at the conceptual level, rhetoric and hermeneutics are coextensive — 'In truth, rhetoric is the overarching concept for everything that has to do with the other' (book p.60); 'It is the same dynamis!' (p.60). At the institutional-pedagogical level, Gadamer admits a displacement: 'I no longer felt that I was at the apex of my philological knowledge' (p.62); he never held a class on rhetoric. The position is therefore: hermeneutics IS rhetoric properly understood, so there is no displacement at the conceptual level — but at the institutional level, Gadamer acknowledges he did not develop a rhetoric pedagogy and that this was a real limitation. Gadamer partially affirms Gross's worry institutionally while denying it conceptually.
key_evidence: Gadamer p.60: 'rhetoric is the overarching concept for everything that has to do with the other'; 'It is the same dynamis!' (HR-02-GADAMER-P5, P7)
Gadamer p.62: 'I no longer felt that I was at the apex of my philological knowledge' (HR-02-GADAMER-T7)
Gadamer T7 synthesis: institutional-level partial agreement with Gross

sub_disagreement_DG6a.label: Bröcker vs. Schalk transcript variant at GA 18 110 — Gross corrects Michalski editorially

contributors_on_each_side.Gross: follows Bröcker reading: 'die konkrete Funktion der aristotelischen Rhetorik'
contributors_on_each_side.Michalski: follows Schalk reading: 'die konkrete Funktion der aristotelischen Logic'

sub_disagreement_DG6a.claim: Note 1 of Gross IV acknowledges Michalski as Klostermann editor of GA 18 and identifies a textual variant: the Bröcker transcript reads 'Sofern man vergißt, nach der konkreten Funktion der aristotelischen Rhetorik zu fragen' but Michalski follows Schalk who reads 'Sofern man vergißt, nach der konkreten Funktion der aristotelischen Logic zu fragen.' Gross sides with Bröcker as 'making more sense' in context. The variant is conceptually important: 'forgetting to ask about the concrete function of Aristotelian Rhetoric/Logic' is a different claim. This is a non-trivial philological position Gross takes against the volume editor (Michalski himself contributes Ch 3).
sub_disagreement_DG6a.productive_for_dissertation: philological note: Gross's preferred reading aligns with the volume's titular thesis (rhetoric as Heidegger's central concern in SS 1924); Michalski's editorial choice is comparatively conservative. Dissertation work citing GA 18 110 should flag the variant.

sub_disagreement_DG6b.label: Gadamer 'missed' Schleiermacherian / Lutheran Affektenlehre reclamation Gross calls for

contributors_on_each_side.Gross: Gadamer 'chooses not to reclaim for rhetoric the doctrine of affections (Affektenlehre) as taught by the likes of Luther or Schleiermacher' — this declining is the 'depoliticizing' move
contributors_on_each_side.Gadamer: Affektenlehre is not a Gadamer topic; the interview does not address it

sub_disagreement_DG6b.claim: Gross's Section IV develops Luther's Affektenlehre as the secret history of the hermeneutics of facticity (via Dockhorn 1966). Gadamer's interview neither affirms nor denies this Lutheran genealogy. The disagreement is therefore by-omission: Gross's Lutheran-rhetorical-theological genealogy is offered as the substantive recovery Gadamer declined; Gadamer's silence on the topic is itself a position.
sub_disagreement_DG6b.productive_for_dissertation: the Affektenlehre genealogy is the dissertation-actionable bridge: a Lutheran-rhetorical-theological reading of pathos preserves what Gadamer's hermeneutics lost.

disagreements.synthesis: DG6 is the volume's most direct intra-volume engagement: Gross's Section I interrogates Gadamer, and Ch 2 (Gadamer interview) is the response. The disagreement resolves at TWO different levels: at the conceptual level, Gadamer's claim ('rhetoric is the overarching concept') and Gross's claim (rhetoric as ontological medium) are compatible — both make rhetoric/hermeneutics coextensive. At the institutional-substantive level, Gross's loss-thesis stands: T&M did not develop the Affektenlehre genealogy, and the modern speech-act tradition inherits an impoverished disposition. Gadamer himself partially affirms this at p.62 ('I no longer felt that I was at the apex of my philological knowledge'). The most generative reading takes Gadamer's bewährt-pathos doctrine (DG5) as the move that PARTIALLY recovers what T&M proper had elided.
disagreements.dissertation_relevance: DG6 is essential for any dissertation that wants to position itself in the Heidegger-Gadamer hermeneutic-rhetorical neighborhood. The institutional-conceptual two-level resolution is the dissertation-actionable lever: conceptually align with Gadamer (rhetoric/hermeneutics coextensive), institutionally side with Gross (the rhetorical pedagogy must be developed). The Affektenlehre genealogy (Dockhorn, Luther, Schleiermacher) is Gross's substantive recovery and the dissertation-actionable bridge between Heideggerian rhetoric and theological-rhetorical tradition.

disagreements.topic: Phenomenology as philology vs. phenomenology as protopolitical — how is GA 18 to be read?

position_a.label: Phenomenology AS philology — methodologically authoritative philological reading of GA 18
position_a.claim: Heidegger's SS 1924 lecture course engages in philology in a rigorously academic sense — measured by enlistment of multiple philologists (Jaeger, Diels, Spengel, Bonitz, Themistius, Simplicius, Nietzsche), application of genuinely philological methods (lexicology, etymology, authenticity criticism), and centering of the original Greek text and its concepts. Heidegger 'explicitly rejects the title of philosophy in favor of philology even for this region that exceeds the horizon of classical philology' (book p.72). Philology in Heidegger's sense is a necessary element of hermeneutic phenomenology — the element with which hermeneutic phenomenology takes into account the leading function of speech in the dominance of the interpretedness of Dasein. Michalski's editorial status (GA 18 editor for Klostermann 2002) gives this framing scholarly weight.
key_evidence: Michalski p.67-72: rigorous philology (HR-03-MICHALSKI-P1)
Michalski p.72: Heidegger 'explicitly rejects the title of philosophy in favor of philology' (HR-03-MICHALSKI-P3)
Michalski p.76-77: philology as necessary element of hermeneutic phenomenology (HR-03-MICHALSKI-P5)
Michalski P8 status: methodologically authoritative for all subsequent readers (editor's authority)

position_b.label: Phenomenology as protopolitical — GA 18 as rhetorical protopolitics genesis text
position_b.claim: Heidegger's 1923-24 confrontation with Aristotle's Rhetoric (and secondarily Politics, NE) produces a 'rhetorical protopolitics' equiprimordial with the threefold definition of the human. Rhetoric is not a side-room of fundamental ontology but constitutive of it at the level of the everyday speech-situation. The pre-Marburg formation (Kriegsnotsemester 1919, WS 1920-21) is read as already politically motivated; GA 18 is the genesis text of Heidegger's rhetorical-political project, with Arendt's Human Condition as the protopolitical strand's recovered afterlife. Kisiel's table on p.149 implicitly treats GA 18 as PRIMARILY POLITICAL — the philological exercise is in service of the protopolitical-rhetorical reading, not its constraint.
key_evidence: Kisiel p.131-133: rhetorical protopolitics equiprimordial with threefold definition (HR-06-KISIEL-P1)
Kisiel p.139-141: GA 18 §§45f, 122f, 241 as protopolitical layer (HR-06-KISIEL-P1)
Kisiel p.146: ethos and pathos as constitutive for legein itself (GA 18 165) (HR-06-KISIEL-P7)
Michalski's recognition of the tension (HR-03-MICHALSKI-T5): 'Kisiel reads GA 18 as primarily political-historical genesis text, not philological exercise — both readings cite GA 18 110'

disagreements.synthesis: Michalski's editorial framing (he edited GA 18 for Klostermann) constrains how the lectures can be read; Kisiel's reading reaches a different conclusion from the same text. Both readings cite GA 18 110 (Rhetoric-as-hermeneutic formula) but draw different categorial consequences. The disagreement is productive because it surfaces a meta-question: is GA 18 a philological exercise that exceeds classical philology in the direction of dialectic and philosophy (Michalski), or is GA 18 a political-historical genesis text where the philological apparatus serves the protopolitical project (Kisiel)? Michalski's answer would constrain the protopolitical reading by insisting on the philological-methodological discipline; Kisiel's reading would absorb the philological apparatus into the broader political reading. The two readings are not strictly incompatible (Heidegger's procedure IS both philological AND protopolitical), but they prioritize differently.
disagreements.dissertation_relevance: DG7 is methodologically consequential: any dissertation citing GA 18 must declare its reading-protocol. Michalski's reading disciplines the dissertation against political-philosophical over-reading; Kisiel's reading licenses the protopolitical interpretation. The most defensible position takes Michalski's editorial authority as constraint (the philological discipline IS Heidegger's stated method, GA 18 4, 333) while accepting Kisiel's broader political implication (the philological exercise serves the protopolitical reading).

disagreements.topic: BT 178 reception — load-bearing positive endorsement of rhetoric vs. moment of restriction (by-omission for Pöggeler)

position_a.label: BT 178 as positive endorsement — Aristotle's Rhetoric II as 'first systematic hermeneutic of everydayness'
position_a.claim: Heidegger's BT 178: 'Contrary to the traditional [scholastic] orientation, according to which rhetoric is conceived as the kind of thing we learn in school, this work of Aristotle [Rhetoric II] must be taken as the first systematic hermeneutic of the everydayness of Being with one another' — read as a load-bearing positive endorsement. Hyde cites BT 178 multiple times as the anchor for his epideictic-conscience argument. Struever cites BT 178 as epigraph for her Alltäglichkeit-as-timefulness essay. Kisiel cites BT 178 as constitutive for SS 1924 protopolitics. Gross cites BT 178 as Heidegger's own admission of the rhetorical genealogy.
key_evidence: Hyde p.82, p.88, p.95: BT 178 as anchor (HR-04-HYDE-P1, P2, HL1)
Struever p.105 (epigraph): BT 178 as Rhetorik [ist]... die erste systematische Hermeneutik der Alltäglichkeit des Miteinanderseins (HR-05-STRUEVER-P2)
Kisiel p.132: BT 178 as constitutive for SS 1924 protopolitics
Gross Intro p.27: BT 178 cited approvingly as marking the rhetorical genealogy

position_b.label: BT 178 as moment of restriction — confines political to everydayness (das Man / Öffentlichkeit)
position_b.claim: Heidegger's BT §29 reading of Aristotle's Rhetoric as 'first systematic hermeneutic of everydayness' is RESTRICTIVE, not constitutive: Heidegger thereby CONFINES the political to everydayness (das Man / Öffentlichkeit), not extending it to deliberative public assembly. 'Does Heidegger assume the political in general to be confined to everydayness and hence just to the businesslike dealings of the they?' The omission of the rhetorical-deliberative-public dimension is THE RESTRICTION — the title's 'restricted' refers to this omission. Pöggeler's silence on BT 178 / GA 18 110 as a load-bearing positive endorsement is itself a position (VT9 = sub-disagreement DG8a).
key_evidence: Pöggeler p.168: BT §29 confines political to everydayness (HR-07-POGGELER-P2, P7)
Pöggeler does not cite the Bibliography Section A locus 7 (BT §29) as a load-bearing positive endorsement — instead reads it as moment of restriction
Pöggeler T2 (= VT9 in Phase 0): Pöggeler's contrastive omission of the GA 18 110 epigraph cluster

sub_disagreement_DG8a.label: GA 18 110 epigraph cluster — Pöggeler's by-omission disagreement (= VT9 in Phase 0)
sub_disagreement_DG8a.claim: GA 18, 110: 'Die Rhetorik ist nichts anderes als die Auslegung des konkreten Daseins, die Hermeneutik des Daseins selbst.' Gross uses as epigraph (Intro p.1); Struever uses as epigraph (Ch 5 p.105); Hyde takes as license (Ch 4 p.82); Kisiel reads as protopolitical (Ch 6 p.132). Pöggeler does NOT foreground this passage in Ch 7 — its absence is significant. Pöggeler reads BT §29 (which contains substantively similar content) as the moment of restriction. The by-omission disagreement is structural: the volume's most-cited single passage (GA 18 110 — epigraph for Ch 1 and Ch 5) is the passage Pöggeler declines to engage as positive evidence.
sub_disagreement_DG8a.productive_for_dissertation: the GA 18 110 passage IS the volume's center of gravity; Pöggeler's omission marks the structural limit of the restriction thesis (it cannot account for this passage as positive evidence).

disagreements.synthesis: DG8 is the most concentrated textual disagreement in the volume — a single passage (BT 178 / GA 18 110) is the productive site where centrality-cluster and restriction-thesis directly diverge. The four contributors who treat BT 178 as load-bearing positive endorsement use it as anchor (Hyde), epigraph (Struever, Gross), and constitutive evidence (Kisiel). Pöggeler reads the same passage as the moment of restriction. The disagreement cannot be resolved by reading the passage harder — it requires a meta-level interpretive choice about Heidegger's interpretation of 'everydayness': is everydayness (Alltäglichkeit) the rich, time-fraught, political-rhetorical mode Heidegger DISCLOSES (centrality reading), or is everydayness das Man / Öffentlichkeit / Gerede — the inauthentic mode Heidegger CONFINES the political to (restriction reading)? Struever's 'Alltäglichkeit as timefulness' (HR-05-STRUEVER-P2) is the most articulated rebuttal to Pöggeler's confined-everydayness reading: Alltäglichkeit means timefulness, not ordinariness, and the BT 178 endorsement names a positive rhetorical-political mode, not a confined-to-the-they mode.
disagreements.dissertation_relevance: DG8 is dissertation-actionable: any reading of BT 178 must address Pöggeler's restriction reading. Struever's 'Alltäglichkeit-as-timefulness' is the strongest single rebuttal — and the dissertation can extend it by argued textual work on the BT §§27-29 cluster (das Man + Befindlichkeit + Aristotle Rhetoric II reception). The Pöggeler by-omission point (DG8a) is the negative case: any continuity-with-centrality reading of BT 178 must explain why the most-cited single GA 18 passage (110) is invisible in Ch 7's restriction reading.

disagreements.topic: Gross n.1 correcting Michalski editorially at GA 18 110 (Bröcker vs. Schalk transcript variant)
disagreements.phase0_vt: DG6a (sub) elevated to standalone DG9 due to philological consequence

position_a.label: Bröcker reading — 'aristotelischen Rhetorik' (Gross)
position_a.claim: Gross IV Note 1 sides with Bröcker's transcript reading at GA 18 110: 'Sofern man vergißt, nach der konkreten Funktion der aristotelischen Rhetorik zu fragen.' This reading makes the passage's reference to rhetoric explicit — supporting the volume's titular thesis (rhetoric as Heidegger's central concern in SS 1924). Gross flags this against the volume's editorial machinery: 'Schalk reads aristotelischen Logic; the Bröcker reading makes more sense in context.'
key_evidence: Gross IV Note 1: 'GA 18, 110, ed. Mark Michalski (Frankfurt: Klostermann, 2002)' — followed by Bröcker variant note (HR-01-GROSS-B-T8)

position_b.label: Schalk reading — 'aristotelischen Logic' (Michalski's Klostermann edition)
position_b.claim: Michalski's authoritative Klostermann 2002 edition follows Schalk's transcript reading at GA 18 110: 'aristotelischen Logic.' This is the published canonical text. Michalski's editorial choice gives Schalk's reading the status of canonical GA 18 text; Gross's preference for Bröcker is a non-canonical philological dissent.
key_evidence: GA 18 110, ed. Mark Michalski, Klostermann 2002 (Schalk variant)
Note: Michalski's own essay (Ch 3) does NOT thematize this textual variant — silence is implicit endorsement of the edition's reading

disagreements.synthesis: DG9 is unique in the volume: a single textual variant becomes the site of intra-volume editorial disagreement. The variant is conceptually consequential: 'forgetting to ask about the concrete function of Aristotelian Rhetoric/Logic' is a different claim — the Rhetoric-reading aligns with the volume's titular thesis; the Logic-reading is more conservative. Gross's preference for Bröcker is consistent with his (and the volume's) centrality reading; Michalski's Schalk-following is consistent with his philological-conservative methodology (DG7). The disagreement is productive because it stages the methodological conflict (DG7) at the level of a single textual variant.
disagreements.dissertation_relevance: DG9 is a dissertation-actionable philological note: any citation of GA 18 110 must specify which transcript reading is followed. Gross's Bröcker reading aligns with the centrality thesis but is non-canonical; Michalski's Schalk reading is canonical but supports the more conservative restriction-amenable reading. The dissertation can either follow Michalski's canonical text (Schalk) and acknowledge the variant in a footnote, or follow Gross's preferred reading (Bröcker) with explicit philological justification.

disagreements.topic: Struever's 'timefulness' coinage refines or replaces Hyde's epideictic-temporality reading

position_a.label: Alltäglichkeit as timefulness — temporal mode, not ordinariness (Struever)
position_a.claim: Alltäglichkeit, properly understood, means timefulness — not 'ordinariness' but the timely character of practical life, the catalytic agent of temporality, the primary qualification of Miteinandersein. Struever explicitly contests the 'ordinariness' translation, coining 'timefulness' as proper rendering. Blattner's reading of Alltäglichkeit as eroded into 'everydayness, ordinariness, inauthenticity' in BT is partially corrected: in 1924 'extraordinary emphasis on Hellenic political rhetoric as originary matrix is at the same time an emphasis on Alltäglichkeit as timeful, or the solvent of eternity.' The BT 178 endorsement of Aristotle Rhetoric II names Alltäglichkeit-as-timefulness, not Alltäglichkeit-as-ordinariness.
key_evidence: Struever p.110-115 (Section I.3-4): timefulness coinage (HR-05-STRUEVER-P2)
Struever p.121 (Blattner contrast): partial correction of Blattner's erosion-thesis (HR-05-STRUEVER-T1)
Struever p.125: 'a Heideggerian politics of time appears, even if briefly, in SS 1924' (HR-05-STRUEVER-P9)

position_b.label: BT 178 as anchoring epideictic-conscience reading — temporal/spatial restructuring via pathē (Hyde)
position_b.claim: Anger, fear, and pity are not psychological epiphenomena but operations that 'restructure existential temporality and spatiality' — they bring the not-yet of the future close, dilate or contract lived space, and constitute identification. BT 179-182, 228-235 distinguish the temporal/spatial workings of fear from anxiety — same conceptual operation as Aristotle Rhetoric II. The temporal-existential restructuring is the rhetorical-pathic operation Heidegger inherits from Aristotle.
key_evidence: Hyde p.86-88: pathē as temporal-spatial restructuring (HR-04-HYDE-P4)
Hyde BT 178 anchor (HR-04-HYDE-HL1)
Hyde T3 register-acknowledgment: 'Hyde's orator-position is closer to Aristotle's NE phronimos; Gross's is closer to Heidegger's pre-thematic Befindlichkeit'

disagreements.synthesis: Both contributors read BT 178 as load-bearing positive endorsement (DG8 position-a); both read pathē as temporally-existentially operative. The productive divergence is at the translation level: Hyde does not propose 'timefulness' as English rendering, working within standard 'everydayness' translation. Struever's coinage is more aggressive: she contends 'ordinariness' is a wrong translation that obscures the temporal-political mode Heidegger names. The disagreement is generative because it surfaces a translation-stakes question: does the English rendering of Alltäglichkeit shape what kind of rhetorical-political work the term can do?
disagreements.dissertation_relevance: DG10 is dissertation-actionable at the translation register: Struever's 'timefulness' is the most philologically-aggressive rendering of Alltäglichkeit in the volume and addresses a real translation problem ('everydayness' / 'ordinariness' obscures the temporal-political mode). Dissertation work citing BT §27 / §29 / Aristotle Rhetoric II should engage Struever's coinage explicitly. The dissertation can layer Struever's timefulness onto Hyde's epideictic-temporal restructuring without contradiction.

disagreements.topic: Ethos translated into Entschlossenheit (Kisiel) vs. Ruf des Gewissens (Hyde) — which BT vocabulary best translates Aristotelian ethos?

position_a.label: Ethos as Entschlossenheit — deliberative-political-prohairesis register (Kisiel)
position_a.claim: Kisiel's Section V translates Aristotelian ethos into BT's Entschlossenheit (resoluteness, BT §60). Ethos is read in the deliberative-political register: the rhetorician's ethos qua phronesis kai arete kai eunoia (Rhet. 2.1 1378a10) becomes Heidegger's resolute Being-its-Self that enables authentic Being-with. The deliberative-political ethos is constitutive of the protopolitical project. Kisiel's reading emphasizes prohairesis (choice) — the deliberative-political-volitional dimension of ethos.
key_evidence: Kisiel p.146: 'ethos and pathos are constitutive for legein itself' (GA 18 165) — ethos in deliberative-prohairesis register (HR-06-KISIEL-P7)
Kisiel SZ §60 Entschlossenheit translation (HR-06-KISIEL-T10-cross)

position_b.label: Ethos as Ruf des Gewissens — epideictic-existential register (Hyde)
position_b.claim: Hyde's chapter translates Aristotelian ethos into BT's Ruf des Gewissens (call of conscience, BT §§54-60). Ethos is read in the epideictic-existential register: the silent call of conscience is the primordial epideictic showing-forth of the heart of human existence. Phronesis IS Gewissen 'set in motion' (per Taminiaux 1992); the etymological chain phronesis-phrēn (heart) / syn-eidesis / con-scientia confirms the identity. Hyde's reading emphasizes the silent-showing-forth dimension of ethos.
key_evidence: Hyde p.81, p.91: phronesis = Gewissen (HR-04-HYDE-P3)
Hyde p.82, p.88, p.95: call of conscience as primordial epideictic (HR-04-HYDE-P1)

disagreements.synthesis: Both contributors translate Aristotelian ethos into a BT category; both ground the translation in Heideggerian textual evidence (Kisiel via SZ §60 + GA 18 165; Hyde via SZ §§54-60 + Aristotle Rhet. I.3, I.9 + Taminiaux 1992). The divergence reveals each contributor's rhetorical-genre preference: Kisiel emphasizes deliberative-political ethos (Entschlossenheit + prohairesis); Hyde emphasizes epideictic-existential ethos (Ruf des Gewissens). Both readings are textually grounded — the choice between them is a matter of which Aristotelian rhetorical genre best captures the existential-ontological work Heidegger asks of ethos. The disagreement is productive because it surfaces the under-thematized question: when Heidegger translates Aristotle's three modes of persuasion (ethos, pathos, logos) into BT vocabulary, which RHETORICAL GENRE structures the translation? Kisiel's Entschlossenheit is more political-deliberative; Hyde's Ruf des Gewissens is more existential-epideictic.
disagreements.dissertation_relevance: DG11 is dissertation-actionable at the rhetorical-genre level: the dissertation can mine the unresolved question of which Aristotelian genre (deliberative, forensic, epideictic) best maps onto Heideggerian existentialia. The cleanest dissertation move is to treat the three genres as differentiated rhetorical-existential registers — Hyde's epideictic-conscience reading captures one mode; Kisiel's deliberative-Entschlossenheit captures another. The Aristotelian genre-typology can structure a fuller Heideggerian rhetorical anthropology.
